newsitem.title: USA: Motorola signs $58 mln China cellular pact.
newsitem.headline: Motorola signs $58 mln China cellular pact.

text.p: Motorola's Asia Pacific Cellular Infrastructure Group (APCIG) said Tuesday it signed a $58 million contract to manufacture and supply digital cellular infrastructure equipment in China.
Motorola said it signed the contract with China Eastern Communications Co Ltd (Eastcom) and Zhejiang Technical Import and Export Corp (ZTIEC).
The contract is the second Global System for Mobile (GSM) Communications contract involving the three companies.
The agreement enables Eastcom to manufacture and distribute Motorola's GSM cell site equipment to cellular operators in China.
Motorola APCIG will provide Eastcom with related support services, including training and system design, the company said.
Eastcom has been supplying Motorola CIG cellular equipment in China since 1991.

Eastcom became a public company in 1996 and is traded on the Shanghai stock exchange, Motorola said. It said it is China's largest mobile communications product manufacturer and supplier, with a reported business volume of $392 million in 1995.
ZTIEC is a state-owned entity that facilitates high technology import and export agreements for companies and factories located in Zhejiang province.
Motorola provides wireless communications, semiconductors, and advanced electronic systems and services.
